extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, administrators, applicants, and stakeholders interested in NIH grants policy and resources)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page listing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and guidance items relevant to grant applicants, awardees, and research administrators. It aggregates short items pointing to deeper resources on topics like model selection, data management plans, reproducibility, and peer review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential; choose models aligned to the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan required elements (2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format and its simplified required elements when preparing DMS Plans for applicable applications (refer to the linked resource for the full element list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH's Gold Standard Science plan and the new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative aim to encourage a culture that values replication and reproducibility; applicants and awardees should consider replication/reproducibility practices across applications, awards, and highlighted topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes an NIH review-process outcome: applications in the middle third may be scored as competitive but not discussed rather than being discussed in full. Applicants should be aware of this classification and its implications for review outcomes and subsequent actions.
